project.title: DQCP is model-dependent: SU(2) J-Q is weakly first order while large-N remains open
project.hidden_assumption: DQCP has a single yes/no answer about continuity independent of model class.

contradiction.proposition_A: DQCP is a true continuous transition beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm with emergent SO(5) behavior.
contradiction.proposition_B: The SU(2) J-Q DQCP is weakly first order, with pseudo-critical walking behavior.
contradiction.why_not_both: A specific SU(2) J-Q transition cannot be both truly continuous and weakly first order, although other model classes may realize different outcomes.
contradiction.resolution: For SU(2) J-Q the surviving conclusion is weak first order. The stronger claim that all DQCPs are weakly first order is not supported; SU(N>=8) and other classes remain possible continuous cases.

derivation_chain.description: Walking behavior occurs when the beta function lacks a real zero but has nearby complex fixed-point structure.
assumptions: small positive offset from real fixed point

validation.caveat: formula is a phenomenological walking template

derivation_chain.description: Class-11 anticommutation constrains beta-function terms but does not force BKT walking.

validation.logic: real fixed points are not symmetry-forbidden

prior_art_search.impact: SU(2) weak-first-order conclusion relies heavily on existing numerical and theoretical evidence; project increment is convergence and boundary classification.

claims.statement: The SU(2) J-Q DQCP is best classified as weakly first order.
evidence_for: Takahashi L=1024 correlation result favors first order
GATE5 closure repeats SU(2) weak-first-order status
evidence_against: Entanglement evidence confirms Goldstone modes but does not alone distinguish continuous from pseudo-critical first order

claims.statement: DQCP behavior should be treated as a cross-model spectrum, not a single binary answer.
evidence_for: GATE5 states SU(N>=8) may be truly continuous
S4 says weak first order is dynamical and model-specific rather than symmetry-forced
evidence_against: Critical N is estimated rather than closed

claims.statement: All DQCPs are weakly first order by symmetry necessity.
evidence_against: SU(N>=8), loop models, and fermion models remain possible true-continuous cases

claims.statement: Entanglement entropy alone proves the SU(2) J-Q transition is truly continuous.
evidence_against: b approximately 2 confirms Goldstone modes but cannot distinguish SO(5) CFT from pseudo-critical first order
Takahashi finite-size result favors weak first order

predictions.statement: SU(2) J-Q finite-size scaling should show pseudo-critical behavior up to xi between about 448 and 1024 before weak first-order signatures dominate.
predictions.measurement_conditions: Large-scale simulations with correlated observable analysis.

predictions.statement: Increasing N should move DQCP candidates toward a genuinely continuous regime around N_c of order 8-10.
predictions.observable: presence or absence of real RG fixed point and first-order histogram signatures
predictions.measurement_conditions: Compare SU(N) models across N with matched finite-size protocols.

lessons.lesson: A model-specific weak-first-order conclusion should not be promoted to a universal DQCP no-go theorem.
Goldstone-mode evidence and continuity evidence are logically distinct.
When a later numerical result independently resolves a question, project novelty shifts toward synthesis and boundary classification.
